META.role: Models, consumer platforms and AI infrastructure buyer

MUFG.note: MUFG Bank is the operating counterparty, not the listed issuer. Its listed parent Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group has ticker MUFG.

edges.title: Completed Intel equity purchase
edges.detail: Intel reports the sale of approximately 215 million shares to NVIDIA closed on December 26, 2025. An equity financing inflow, not Intel product revenue. This does not prove NVIDIA will manufacture GPUs at Intel.

edges.title: Completed Intel equity purchase
edges.detail: Intel completed the sale of 86,956,522 shares to SoftBank for cash. An equity financing inflow, not semiconductor revenue.

edges.title: Custom AI fabric and Xeon chip framework
edges.detail: Intel and AWS announced co-investment in custom designs, products and wafers, including an AI fabric chip on Intel 18A and custom Xeon 6 on Intel 3. Framework value is not recognized revenue or verified cash paid. Allocation between co-investment and purchases is not disclosed; production completion is not established by this source.

edges.title: NVIDIA compute and networking deployments
edges.detail: A February 2026 partnership covers large-scale CPU deployment, millions of Blackwell/Rubin GPUs and Spectrum-X networking. Hardware deployment roadmap is not a disclosed cash total; do not multiply device counts by invented prices.

edges.status: initial 1 GW binding; up to 6 GW framework
edges.title: AMD GPU purchases
edges.detail: The AMD filing establishes an initial binding purchase commitment equivalent to 1 GW, directly or via authorized purchasers, within the broader 6 GW partnership. Do not label all 6 GW as an unconditional paid order, or attach an unsourced dollar value. The arrow follows the end-customer commitment; fulfillment can run through authorized purchasers.

edges.title: Purchase-linked equity incentive
edges.detail: AMD issued Meta a performance-based warrant. Vesting depends on GPU purchases and other contractual milestones. Direction denotes delivery of a contingent financial right, not cash. As of June 27, 2026 no shares had vested or become exercisable; full exercise is not a completed investment.

edges.title: Expanded AI cloud agreement
edges.detail: CoreWeave announced expanded cloud capacity for Meta through December 2032. The filing says the amount includes new capacity and exercise of an existing capacity option. Not cash paid or annual revenue. Do not mechanically add earlier headline contract/option values, because option overlap is explicit.

edges.title: Optical fiber and connectivity agreement
edges.detail: Corning will supply optical fiber, cable and connectivity for Meta data-center expansion and expand North Carolina capacity. Commitment ceiling, not completed cash payments or current-year revenue.

edges.title: Arizona advanced silicon purchasing
edges.detail: Apple disclosed a multibillion-dollar commitment to TSMC Fab 21 and said production of its chips had begun. Broader Apple silicon procurement: no AI-only dollar allocation. Neither the entire US spending pledge nor all Apple chip purchases equal AI server capex.

edges.title: Advanced packaging capacity support
edges.detail: Apple is investing in the Amkor Arizona packaging facility and says it will be the first and largest customer. It will package TSMC-made Apple silicon. Amkor factory cost is not Apple’s investment amount; no AI-only spending allocation. Source specifically also mentions iPhone chips.

edges.title: Claude uses SpaceX Colossus capacity
edges.detail: Agreement for all Colossus 1 capacity (>220,000 NVIDIA GPUs), expected accessible within that month. Orbital capacity was expressed interest only, not funded construction.

edges.title: SpaceX buys Tesla Megapacks
edges.detail: Recorded in property, plant and equipment. Includes $295M in Q2; do not add Q2 to H1. This disclosure is purchase value, not a separately evidenced cash-settlement schedule.

edges.title: OpenAI contracts Cerebras inference
edges.detail: Issuer June release confirms agreement size and capacity. Do not treat lifetime contract value as recognized or paid revenue.

edges.title: OpenAI finances Cerebras working capital
edges.detail: Separate loan category; not equity, not additional sales revenue. Avoid presenting loan+contract as incremental demand.

edges.title: ASML backs Mistral
edges.detail: Part of €1.7B round, not additive to it. ASML also enters commercial/technical collaboration; fees undisclosed.

edges.title: Samsung takes Mistral stake
edges.detail: Samsung leads Series D and secures strategic equity stake; the full funding round must not be attributed to Samsung alone.

edges.title: Mistral models for Samsung fabs
edges.detail: On-premises models across semiconductor engineering/manufacturing. Shows investor also becoming user; no tracked-dollar loop.

edges.title: Meta invests in Scale
edges.detail: Release gives >$29B Scale valuation, not investment size. Some proceeds distributed to existing equity holders; don't classify entire transaction as operating cash available to Scale.

edges.title: Meta expands data-services relationship
edges.detail: Separate from equity investment; no supplier revenue amount supplied.

edges.title: Microsoft invests in G42
edges.detail: Announcement does not establish settlement schedule. Distinct from jointly supported developer fund.

edges.title: G42 applications on Azure
edges.detail: Investor/customer relationship; no amount or claim that investment funds purchase exact Azure services.

edges.title: OpenAI follow-on equity investment
edges.detail: SoftBank executed the final $10B tranche via Vision Fund 2. This completes the $30B follow-on program; cumulative OpenAI investment is $64.6B. These figures overlap and must not be added.

edges.status: notes issued; proceeds used for OpenAI tranche
edges.title: Senior-note financing for AI investment
edges.detail: Notes were priced September 24 with issuance scheduled September 29. The October 1 update confirms note proceeds funded the $10B OpenAI tranche; other proceeds were for general corporate purposes. Borrowing is not operating revenue.

edges.title: Cerebras hardware and compute customer
edges.detail: Cerebras identified G42 as a significant customer, alongside the separate MBZUAI customer. The percentage describes revenue concentration, not a standalone payment or current-year run rate.

edges.status: warrant issued and exercised in April 2026
edges.title: Customer equity rights
edges.amountLabel: 1,655,975 Class N shares at $0.01 exercise price
edges.detail: The issuer reports an April warrant to G42, fully vested and exercised that month. The arrow denotes an equity right, not cash paid to G42. These are historical pre-IPO Class N shares, not a dollar market value.

cases.title: SpaceXAI: competitor, compute host and power buyer
cases.summary: Anthropic contracts SpaceX compute; SpaceX buys Tesla Megapacks.
cases.insight: One public group can develop rival models and supply compute to another frontier lab, while its physical buildout supports battery demand.
cases.limitation: SpaceX/xAI is one listed parent; Tesla is separate. Capacity commitments and recorded equipment purchases are different measures. No same-dollar loop is demonstrated.

cases.title: Intel: strategic equity meets future chip demand
cases.summary: NVIDIA and SoftBank buy Intel equity while AWS establishes a custom-chip framework.
cases.insight: Equity supports the balance sheet; the AWS relationship is a separate route to possible product and wafer revenue.
cases.limitation: The $5B and $2B purchases are equity, not sales. The framework is not booked revenue, and NVIDIA equity does not establish a GPU foundry order.

cases.title: Meta: compute demand, warrants and data services
cases.summary: Meta contracts GPUs, cloud and optical connectivity while expanding its Scale relationship.
cases.insight: Meta spending reaches multiple hardware and cloud suppliers; AMD grants contingent equity rights in the opposite direction.
cases.limitation: The 6GW AMD framework is broader than the initial 1GW binding purchase. Warrants are not cash. CoreWeave option overlap prevents adding every contract headline together.

cases.title: Apple: silicon and packaging behind local AI
cases.summary: Apple supports TSMC Arizona silicon and Amkor packaging capacity.
cases.insight: On-device AI and Private Cloud Compute connect to manufacturing capacity as well as model partnerships.
cases.limitation: Disclosures cover broader Apple products, including iPhones. No AI-only spending allocation is available. Amkor facility cost is not Apple investment, and Google collaboration has no payment arrow.

cases.title: Cerebras: customers also supply capital
cases.kind: Contract demand, customer loans and equity rights
cases.summary: OpenAI provides a loan and contracts inference; G42 generates revenue and receives customer equity rights.
cases.insight: Customer financing can help a supplier build capacity before service revenue arrives; customer equity rights add another economic connection.
cases.limitation: The multiyear contract, loan, annual revenue concentration and non-cash shares are not additive. G42 and OpenAI are distinct customers; the evidence does not trace identical dollars.

cases.title: From bond markets and chip fabs to AI labs
cases.summary: SoftBank funds OpenAI with note proceeds; ASML and Samsung back Mistral, and Samsung adopts its models.
cases.insight: AI capital comes from debt investors and industrial companies as well as hyperscalers. Some backers also become customers or suppliers.
cases.limitation: These are separate documented paths, not one closed loop. SoftBank tranche, program and cumulative totals overlap. Individual Samsung/Mistral fees are undisclosed; bank debt is not lab revenue.
